title: Pharmacokinetics and Initial Bolus Dosing of Furosemide in Children on ECMO.
abstract: Extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO) is an established technology that provides life-saving mechanical support for critically ill children. In these children, fluid overload is commonly treated with furosemide; however, optimal dosing of furosemide is unknown in children supported with ECMO because ECMO may alter furosemide exposure. In this work, human blood-primed ex vivo experiments quantified red blood cell partitioning and extraction of furosemide by the ECMO circuit. Furosemide partitioned into red blood cells but was not extracted by ECMO circuits. These data then parameterized a pediatric physiologically based pharmacokinetic (PBPK) model of furosemide in children with and without ECMO. Next, plasma furosemide concentrations from 10 critically ill children supported by ECMO were used to evaluate PBPK model performance, with the optimized model achieving average fold error and absolute average fold error of 1.02 and 1.67, respectively. The optimized PBPK model also predicted that ECMO increases apparent volume of distribution by a median of > 30% in neonates and infants. Finally, population PBPK simulations with the optimized PBPK model provided initial bolus doses that most rapidly achieve steady-state plasma furosemide concentrations with and without ECMO. These calibrated initial bolus doses achieved steady-state plasma furosemide concentrations > 3 h faster than continuous infusions without an initial bolus dose, and this improvement was most pronounced in neonates and infants on ECMO. Overall, this work supports comparatively larger initial bolus doses for neonates and infants on ECMO, and provides calibrated initial bolus doses based on plasma exposure for critically ill children.

title: Comparison of clinical outcomes in carbapenemase-producing and non-carbapenemase-producing carbapenem-resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae bacteraemia.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Carbapenem-resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae (CRKP) infections are associated with substantial morbidity and mortality. However, clinical outcomes associated with different resistance mechanisms remain inconsistently reported. This study aimed to compare the clinical outcomes of bacteraemia caused by carbapenemase-producing CRKP (CP-CRKP) and non-carbapenemase-producing CRKP (non-CP-CRKP). METHODS: This single-centre retrospective cohort study enrolled adult patients with CRKP bacteraemia in Taiwan between January 2012 and December 2022. Polymerase chain reaction was used to detect carbapenemase genes in all isolates, including Klebsiella pneumoniae carbapenemase (KPC), New Delhi Metallo-β-lactamase (NDM), Verona integron-encoded metallo-β-lactamase (VIM), imipenemase metallo-β-lactamase (IMP), and oxacillinase-48-type carbapenemase (OXA-48). The primary outcomes were 14-day, 28-day mortality, in-hospital mortality, and prolonged hospitalisation. RESULTS: A total of 381 patients with CRKP bacteraemia were included, of whom 294 (77.2%) had CP-CRKP and 87 (22.8%) had non-CP-CRKP infections. bla CONCLUSIONS: Among patients with CRKP bacteraemia, CP-CRKP was not independently associated with mortality but was independently associated with prolonged hospitalisation. These findings highlight that the identification of carbapenemase production has a role in predicting a prolonged clinical course.

title: Low-dose Liposomal Amphotericin B for Antifungal Prophylaxis in Prolonged Neutropenia Patients
sourceName: Haikou Affiliated Hospital of Central South University Xiangya School of Medicine
abstract: This is a single-center, single-arm, observational clinical study evaluating the efficacy and safety of low-dose liposomal amphotericin B (50 mg/day, intravenous, once daily) for the prevention of invasive fungal infections in adult patients (aged 18-75 years) with hematological malignancies who develop prolonged neutropenia (absolute neutrophil count ≤0.5×10\^9/L, expected to last \>7 days) and are at high risk for invasive fungal disease. Participants are those who, per the treating physician's routine clinical decision, have been initiated on liposomal amphotericin B prophylaxis at 50 mg/day due to intolerance or toxicity to other antifungal agents. The primary outcome is the incidence of proven or probable invasive fungal disease. Secondary outcomes include incidence of pneumonia, persistent unexplained fever \>4 days, use of additional systemic antifungal therapy, and adverse events. A total of 30 participants will be enrolled. Data will be collected at baseline, during treatment, and within 7 days after treatment completion.

title: A Phase 3 Efficacy and Safety Study of Fosmanogepix for the Treatment of Adult Participants With Candidemia and/or Invasive Candidiasis.
abstract: The purpose of this clinical trial is to learn about the safety and effects of the study medicine (called Fosmanogepix) for the potential treatment of candidemia and/or invasive candidiasis, a life-threatening fungal infection caused by several species of yeast called Candida. The study is seeking patients who have a diagnosis of candidemia and/or invasive candidiasis. Two-thirds of all patients will receive the study medication fosmanogepix Intravenous (IV) infusion followed by optional fosmanogepix tablets. One-third of all patients will receive a standard of care regimen of caspofungin Intravenous (IV) infusion followed by optional fluconazole capsules. Fosmanogepix or caspofungin will first be given as an Intravenous (IV) infusion directly into a vein in the arm each day at the study clinic. Fosmanogepix tablets or fluconazole capsules will be taken orally by mouth daily either at the study clinic, or at home if patients are well enough to be discharged from the hospital. The treatment effect in patients receiving fosmanogepix to those receiving caspofungin/ fluconazole will be compared. The primary aim is to show that fosmanogepix is not inferior (not worse) to caspofungin/ fluconazole with a noninferiority margin of 15%. The duration of study treatment and number of study visits will vary depending on how long the patient will be treated for the infection. Treatment will continue for a maximum of 6 weeks depending on when the infection is cleared and whether other symptoms related to the infection have improved. There will also be a follow-up visit 6 weeks after the study treatment was stopped.

title: Study of Posaconazole Prophylaxis in Patients Receiving Hematopoietic Stem Cell Allograft (Allo-HSC) at High Risk of Invasive Fungal Infection (IFI)
abstract: Patients receiving an allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplant (allo-CSH) are at high risk of infection, particularly of fungal origin. Until the 2018 recommendations of the 6th European Conference on Infections in Leukemia (ECIL6), primary prophylaxis of invasive fungal infections (IFI), in allograft patients, was based on the administration of fluconazole until D100. Due to changes in transplantation practices (alternative donor transplantation, sequential transplantation, etc.) and changes in microbiological ecology (increased incidence of IFIs caused by filamentous germs such as aspergillosis and mycormycosis), fluconazole prophylaxis is now sometimes suboptimal. It is therefore recommended that patients at high risk of developing IFIs should be given azole molecules with activity against filamentous agents as primary prophylaxis during the first 3 months after transplantation. Posaconazole is often under-dosed (below the minimum effective concentration). It therefore seems essential to carry out a prospective study with close \[C\]min dosing in the specific situation of allograft patients, a population that appears to be at risk of underdosing in the light of initial retrospective analysis results.

title: The PRECISION Partners Platform (P3) Study
abstract: Infections of the lungs are the most common problem for people with Cystic Fibrosis (CF), but also are significant in people with other lung conditions known generally as chronic suppurative lung diseases (CSLD), which can also cause recurrent chest infections. Some of the most common and severe infections are caused by Pseudomonas aeruginosa (Pa), Staphylococcus aureus (Sa), and Aspergillus fumigatus (Af). It is important to detect these early, in order to treat them and prevent damage to the lungs. At the moment we rely on sputum culture or cough swabs, however, some people (for example small children or those with less severe disease) are not able to provide sputum, and cough swabs are less accurate. Additionally, although modulators such as Kaftrio and Ivacaftor have had significant positive effects on most people with CF taking them, these people often find they no longer produce sputum, and therefore we are not able to test for infections in the same way we did before. Studies have shown that although some people have fewer infections after starting modulators, they generally don't disappear altogether, and therefore we still need a reliable way to test for them. Furthermore, we have seen that some people react differently to certain infections, and people with more than one infection simultaneously, also respond differently to these infections. We would like to find new, reliable, easy and acceptable ways of testing for infections that does not require sputum and are acceptable for patients in order to detect, monitor and treat lung infections early. Additionally, we would like to better understand what causes the differing responses patients have to infections, in order to see if there are new ways we can target treatments. The study is being undertaken in multiple centres across the UK in order to recruit a larger, more diverse and representative group of participants, than we would be able to achieve from one centre alone.

title: Burden of Infections and Antimicrobial Resistance in Neonatal Intensive Care Units in Argentina (PREV-AR NICU): A National Point-Prevalence Study
abstract: PREV-AR NICU was a national, multicenter, cross-sectional point-prevalence study conducted in 58 neonatal intensive care units (NICUs) in Argentina during April 2026. All patients present in a participating NICU during a 24-hour period were included. Active infection was classified as infection without sepsis, probable sepsis, confirmed sepsis, or septic shock. Colonization by multidrug-resistant organisms (MDRO) was assessed by rectal and nasal swabs. Patients were followed for in-NICU mortality. Mixed-effects logistic regression was used to identify independent predictors of infection and mortality.

title: Computational and in vitro evaluation of a purified oxazine-pyridine derivative from endophytic Alternaria alternata as a potential antifungal candidate.
abstract: The growing difficulty of treating fungal infections has intensified the search for chemically distinct antifungal leads from underexplored microbial sources. The present study investigated an endophytic fungal isolate from Ziziphus mauritiana as a potential source of bioactive secondary metabolites. Cultural and microscopic characteristics, including colony morphology, septate hyphae, and muriform conidia, were consistent with the genus Alternaria, while ITS rDNA sequencing, BLAST analysis, and phylogenetic inference identified the isolate as Alternaria alternata. The fungus was cultivated in modified Czapek Dox broth, and its crude ethyl acetate extract was screened for antibacterial, antifungal, cytotoxic, and phytotoxic activity. The extract showed its most notable effect against fungal pathogens, reaching approximately 70% growth inhibition against Candida glabrata at 1000 µg mL

title: Trial Endpoints for Candidemia and Invasive Candidiasis: Consensus Recommendations by the Mycoses Study Group Education & Research Consortium and European Confederation of Medical Mycology.
sourceName: Clinical infectious diseases : an official publication of the Infectious Diseases Society of America
abstract: Invasive candidiasis (IC) remains the most common invasive mycosis world-wide, responsible for a wide range of infections that can range from superficial mucosal infections to life-threatening systemic diseases. Clinical trials of antifungal agents for IC are pivotal to its management. Therapeutic responses in these trials are currently based on consensus criteria initially presented by the Mycoses Study Group (MSG) and the European Organization for Research and the Treatment of Cancer (EORTC) in 2008. These 2008 definitions originally described by Segal et al are still employed by both investigators and regulatory agencies when evaluating antifungal drug efficacy and patient outcomes. However, advances in clinical mycology, the change in epidemiology of Candida infections due to the increase in non-albicans Candida species, and the increase in newer antifungal agents currently under development require a revision of these criteria to ensure appropriate and standardized adjudication of patient outcomes and to accurately capture responses to newer therapeutic regimens and modern interventions. Therefore, the European Confederation of Medical Mycology (ECMM) and Mycoses Study Group Education and Research Consortium (MSGERC) have decided to revise the criteria to be used for future studies.

title: A Phase 1b/2 Trial of the Safety and Microbiological Activity of Bacteriophage Therapy in Cystic Fibrosis Subjects Colonized With Pseudomonas Aeruginosa
sourceName: National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases (NIAID)
abstract: This is a phase 1b/2 study of a single dose of intravenous (IV) bacteriophage in males and non-pregnant females, at least 18 years old, diagnosed with Cystic Fibrosis (CF). This clinical trial is designed to assess the safety and microbiological activity of bacteriophage product Walter Reed Army Institute of Research- PAM-Cystic Fibrosis1 (WRAIR-PAM-CF1), directed at Pseudomonas aeruginosa in clinically stable CF individuals chronically colonized with P. aeruginosa. WRAIR-PAM-CF1 is a 4 component anti-pseudomonal bacteriophage mixture containing between 4 x 10\^7 and 4 x 10\^9 Plaque Forming Units (PFU) of bacteriophage. Enrollment will occur at up to 20 clinical sites in the United States. In stage 1, two eligible subjects will be assigned to each of the three dosing arms receiving a single dosage of the IV bacteriophage therapy (4 x 10\^7 PFU, 4 x 10\^8 PFU, and 4 x 10\^9 PFU; total of 6 sentinel subjects), followed by 30 plus or minus 7 days observation period. If no Serious Adverse Events (SAEs)(related to the study product) are identified during the 96 hours after bacteriophage administration for all Sentinel Subjects in Stage 1, the study will proceed to Stage 2. In Stage 2a, 32 subjects will be enrolled into one of 4 arms (placebo IV, 4 x 10\^7 PFU, 4 x 10\^8 PFU, and 4 x 10\^9 PFU) in a 1:1:1:1 allocation. An interim analysis will be performed after all subjects have completed follow up visit 5 on Day 8+3 to select the IV bacteriophage dose with the most favorable safety and microbiological activity profile. During Stage 2b, subjects will be randomized into the bacteriophage (dose selected based on Interim Analysis following Stage 2a) or placebo arm. The final sample size is expected to be up to 72 subjects total with up to 25 subjects in the placebo arm and up to 25 subjects in the Stage 2b bacteriophage dose.

sourceName: National Institutes of Health Clinical Center (CC)
abstract: Background: * Idiopathic CD4+ lymphocytopenia (ICL) is a condition in which there is a decreased level of CD4+ lymphocytes (a type of white blood cell), which can lead to opportunistic infections or autoimmune disorders and diseases. Objectives: * To characterize the natural history with regard to CD4+ T cell count and onset of infection, malignancy, and autoimmunity. * To describe the immunological status of patients affected by ICL while providing the best possible standard therapy to eradicate opportunistic infections. * To establish the timeline of CD4 lymphocytopenia, with particular focus on defining subgroups of patients according to the decline, stabilization, or rise of CD4+ T cell counts over time. * To characterize the opportunistic infections that occur in ICL patients at microbiologic and molecular levels. * To characterize the immunophenotype and possible genetic immunodeficiency causes of ICL. * To determine whether measurable immunologic parameters correlate with the development of opportunistic infections or other comorbidities such as lymphoma in patients with ICL. * To determine whether there is any association between ICL and autoimmunity. * To determine CD4+ T cell turnover, survival, functionality, and cytokine responsiveness in ICL patients. Eligibility: * Patients 2 years of age and older with an absolute CD4 count less than 300 in children 6 years or older and adults or less than 20% of T cells in children younger than 6 on two occasions at least 6 weeks apart. * Patients with negative results of HIV testing by ELISA, Western Blot, and viral load. * Patients must not have underlying immunodeficiency conditions, be receiving cytotoxic chemotherapy (anti-cancer drugs that kill cells), or have cancer. Design: * At the initial visit to the National Institutes of Health, the following evaluations will be conducted: * Personal and family medical histories. * Physical examination, including rheumatology evaluation and other consultations as medically indicated (e.g., dermatology, pulmonology, ophthalmology, imaging studies). * Blood samples for analysis of red and white blood cell counts, liver function, immune hormones, and antibody and autoantibody levels, white blood cell growth and function, and DNA. * Urinalysis and urine pregnancy testing for female patients of childbearing age. * Evaluation and treatment of active infections as medically indicated, including biopsies, buccal swabs, pulmonary function tests, and imaging studies. * Follow-up visits will take place approximately every 12 months or more frequently if indicated, and will continue for a minimum of 4 years and a maximum of 10 years. * Evaluations at follow-up will include blood samples (i.e., CBC with differential, biochemical profile, HIV testing, etc.) and urinalysis and rheumatology consults.

title: Clinicobacteriological profile, Mortality Predictors and Antimicrobial Resistance in Necrotising Soft Tissue Infections: A prospective study.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Necrotising soft tissue infections (NSTIs) are rapidly progressive infections requiring prompt diagnosis and management. This study assessed predictors of mortality, microbiological spectrum, antimicrobial resistance patterns, and differences between polymicrobial and monomicrobial NSTIs in a prospective manner. METHODS: This study enrolled patients aged 15 years or older with clinically suspected NSTIs who presented between March 2022 and February 2023. Clinical, laboratory, surgical, and outcome data were collected. Tissue and pus samples were processed for aerobic and anaerobic cultures. Antimicrobial susceptibility testing was performed according to CLSI guidelines. Mortality-associated factors were analysed using univariate analysis, binary logistic regression, and survival analysis. RESULTS: Eighty-seven patients were included, predominantly male (87.3%), with a median age of 47.5 years. Extremities were most commonly affected. The mortality rate of this cohort was 25.3%. Polymicrobial infections predominated (49.4%), while monomicrobial NSTIs were associated with higher mortality (p = 0.022). Gram-negative organisms, particularly Acinetobacter baumannii and Escherichia coli, were the most frequent pathogens. Obligate anaerobes were significantly associated with polymicrobial infections. Chronic liver disease (p = 0.003) and systemic toxicity (p = 0.018) independently predicted mortality, whereas higher haemoglobin levels were protective. High antimicrobial resistance was observed, including carbapenem-resistant A. baumannii and Enterobacterales. Among the anaerobes, resistance to clindamycin and cefoxitin, along with reduced susceptibility to metronidazole, was reported. CONCLUSION: NSTIs remain associated with substantial mortality, especially in monomicrobial infections due to multidrug-resistant Gram-negative pathogens. Early recognition, prompt surgery, and region-specific empirical antimicrobial therapy are crucial for improving outcomes.

title: Evaluate the Efficacy and Safety of Ruxolitinib on Hair Regrowth in Patients With Autoimmune Polyendocrinopathy Candidiasis Ectodermal Dystrophy (APECED)-Associated Alopecia Areata
sourceName: National Institutes of Health Clinical Center (CC)
abstract: Background: Autoimmune polyendocrinopathy candidiasis ectodermal dystrophy (APECED) is a problem of the immune system. In people with APECED, the immune system makes a mistake and attacks the body. Some people with APECED have a type of hair loss called alopecia areata (AA). No drugs are approved to treat AA. Objective: To see if a study drug (ruxolitinib) can help hair regrowth in people with APECED-associated AA and if it can improve other symptoms caused by the immune system s attack to the body. Eligibility: People aged 12 to 65 years with APECED and severe AA. Design: Participants will be in this study for up to 10 months. They will have 5 in-person visits and 6 televisits, each about 4 weeks apart. One in-person visit may be up to a 10-day stay in the hospital. The first in-person visit will include screening. Participants will have a physical exam. They will have blood tests. Photographs may be taken of their skin. They will answer questions about their quality of life. title: Farm-originated Antimicrobial Resistance Modeling: Exploring Humans-to-Animal Dissemination
abstract: Antimicrobial resistance is a major public health issue. Methicillin resistance in Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) is one of the indicators that is monitored particularly closely. In animals, pig farms, among others, have been identified as reservoirs of MRSA, with a risk of transmission to humans, particularly to individuals in direct contact with livestock. In France, the prevalence of MRSA in pig farms has increased markedly in recent years. While cross-species transmission between pigs and humans in professional settings is well-documented, the temporal dynamics, the actual incidence of acquisition, and the associated determinants remain insufficiently characterized in France. Adopting a "One Health" approach, this project aims to gain a better understanding of the mechanisms by which MRSA spreads between animal and human subpopulations and to incorporate these insights into a mathematical modeling framework.

title: Population Pharmacokinetics and Model-Informed Precision Dosing of Colistin Sulfate in Critically Ill Patients with Carbapenem-Resistant Gram-Negative Infections: A Prospective Pharmacokinetic-Pharmacodynamic Study.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Independently evaluated population pharmacokinetic models and clinically derived pharmacokinetic/pharmacodynamic targets for colistin sulfate remain limited. We aimed to develop and evaluate a model, explore an efficacy threshold, and construct a research model-informed precision dosing calculator. METHODS: This prospective study included 55 critically ill patients with microbiologically confirmed infection caused by carbapenem-resistant Gram-negative bacteria (CR-GNB) for model development and 15 with suspected CR-GNB infection without microbiological confirmation for independent evaluation of concentration predictions. Plasma concentrations were measured by validated ultra-performance liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry. Modeling used nonlinear mixed-effects modeling software (NONMEM). Logistic regression and receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis assessed efficacy predictors and the exploratory threshold. Monte Carlo simulations evaluated probability of target attainment (PTA). RESULTS: A two-compartment model with creatinine clearance (CrCL) as a covariate on clearance (CL) best described the data (typical CL = 6.67 × (CrCL/76.9) CONCLUSION: This study provides a pharmacokinetic model with preliminary independent predictive evaluation, an exploratory exposure threshold, and an open-access research dosing calculator. Prospective multicenter validation is required before clinical implementation.

title: CONTinuous Infusion Versus Intermittent Dosing of ceftaZidime/AVIbactam in Critically Ill Patients
abstract: Ceftazidime/avibactam (CZA) is an essential treatment option for managing infections caused by multidrug-resistant (MDR) gram-negative (G-) bacteria, including Klebsiella pneumoniae OXA-48 and carbapenem-resistant Pseudomonas aeruginosa. Critically ill intensive care unit (ICU) patients frequently exhibit altered pharmacokinetics (PK) of CZA, potentially compromising optimal PK/pharmacodynamic (PD) target attainment with standard dosing regimens. This study compares the efficacy of continuous infusion (CI) versus conventional intermittent dosing (ID) of CZA in critically ill ICU patients with severe infections caused by K. pneumoniae OXA-48 or P. aeruginosa. This single-centre, randomized, open-label trial will be conducted at a tertiary care hospital within the University Hospital Centre in Zagreb, Croatia, with a 1:1 allocation ratio. One hundred forty critically ill ICU patients requiring CZA treatment will be randomized to receive either ID (2 g/0.5 g every 8 hours over 2 hours) or an equivalent dose in CI (6 g/1.5 g continuously over 24 hours). The primary outcome is the microbiological success rate. Secondary outcomes include clinical success rate, time to symptom improvement, length of ICU and hospital stay, 28-day all-cause mortality, pathogen recurrence rate, time to weaning from mechanical ventilation, cumulative vasoactive-inotropic score, adverse events, and the ratio of ceftazidime plasma concentration to the pathogen's minimum inhibitory concentration (C/MIC). This trial seeks to provide evidence on the optimal administration strategy for CZA in critically ill ICU patients with severe infections due to MDR G- pathogens.

title: Bloodstream Infections After Cardiac Surgery: Pathogen Distribution, Antimicrobial Resistance, and a Nomogram Prediction Model.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Postoperative bloodstream infection (BSI) is a severe complication following cardiac surgery, associated with significant mortality. This study aims to characterize pathogen profiles, antimicrobial resistance and independent risk factors for BSI in a Chinese cardiac surgery cohort. METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study of postoperative BSI in patients who underwent cardiac surgery at the First Affiliated Hospital of Nanjing Medical University from January 2019 to December 2024. Patients who developed postoperative BSI were identified and a 1:1 propensity score matched analysis were performed to adjust for baseline characteristics of patients. Univariate and multivariate analysis were applied to identify independent risk factors for postoperative BSI. R software was used to construct a prediction nomogram, followed by internal validation. RESULTS: During the study, a total of 10,007 patients underwent heart surgery, and 164 pairs of patients were successfully matched using propensity score matching. Gram-negative bacteria were the most common pathogens (64.1%), followed by Fungi (18.2%) and Gram-positive bacteria (17.6%). Among CONCLUSION: Postoperative BSI in cardiac surgery patients is associated with high mortality. A nomogram based on impaired cardiac function (NYHA II-IV), pulmonary infection, emergency surgery, CABG, CRRT and postoperative ICU stay ≥14 d displayed high accuracy and consistency in predicting the risk of postoperative BSI. These results facilitate early risk stratification and guide preventive strategies in high-risk cardiac surgical patients.

title: Population pharmacokinetics of oseltamivir and oseltamivir carboxylate in critically ill adults receiving veno-venous extracorporeal membrane oxygenation without renal replacement therapy - an ASAP ECMO study.
abstract: OBJECTIVES: To characterise the population pharmacokinetics of oseltamivir and oseltamivir carboxylate in critically ill adults receiving veno-venous extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (VV-ECMO) without renal replacement therapy (RRT), and to compare oseltamivir carboxylate exposure with an exploratory exposure-response threshold and published pharmacokinetic data. METHODS: This multinational ASAP ECMO analysis included 8 critically ill adults receiving oseltamivir 75 mg every 12 hours during VV-ECMO. Serial blood samples were collected over a dosing interval, and oseltamivir and oseltamivir carboxylate concentrations were measured using a validated assay. Population pharmacokinetic modelling was performed in Monolix using an integrated parent drug-metabolite model. RESULTS: Fifty-eight plasma concentration-time points were available for analysis. The cohort was relatively young and 63% had augmented renal clearance (ARC). A one-compartment model best described both oseltamivir and oseltamivir carboxylate, with a transit compartment required to account for delayed metabolite formation. Median oseltamivir carboxylate exposure was generally comparable to values reported in healthy adults and critically ill patients receiving standard dosing. Median oseltamivir carboxylate area under the concentration-time curve from 0-12 hours (AUC CONCLUSIONS: Marked variability and lower exposure were observed in adults receiving VV-ECMO without RRT, particularly ARC patients. Higher doses may be required in ARC patients, but the optimal dosing regimen remains undefined. Routine dose escalation is not supported by current evidence.

abstract: Intra-abdominal candidiasis is the most frequent candidiasis infection after candidemia. The studies that have positioned echinocandins as the first therapeutic option in candidiasis have been carried out mainly in patients with candidemia. Peritoneal concentrations of caspofungin, micafungin and anidulafungin are clearly above the MICs of most Candida spp but are below the threshold for selection of resistant mutants, which has been argued by some researchers as a risk for the control of intra-abdominal infections with poor control of the focus and selection of resistant mutants, observed in Candida spp isolates at the peritoneal level in relation to isolates at the blood culture level. Rezafungin, with its special pharmacokinetics, achieves higher tissue concentrations, including hepato-splenic and other abdominal organs, than the other echinocandins. Experimental studies have confirmed that the concentration of rezafungin at the level of the inflammatory focus in abdominal infections is higher than in the surrounding healthy tissue and higher than those achieved by micafungin. Finally, the biofilm activity of rezafungin is very high, clearly superior to fluconazole and possibly higher than that of other echinocandins.

title: Successful application of low-dose regional citrate combined with nafamostat mixed anticoagulation in CRRT for patients with liver failure: a retrospective case series study of 11 patients.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: To investigate the clinical efficacy, safety and operational feasibility of a low-dose regional citrate anticoagulation (RCA) combined with low-dose nafamostat mesylate (NM) mixed anticoagulation regimen in continuous renal replacement therapy (CRRT) for patients with liver failure, so as to provide clinical reference for the selection of CRRT anticoagulation strategies for such special high-risk critically ill patients. METHOD: A retrospective case series study was conducted. Eleven patients with liver failure who received CRRT in the Department of Critical Care Medicine, Zhongnan Hospital of Wuhan University were enrolled. All patients were treated with CVVHDF mode and uniformly implemented the low-dose citrate combined with nafamostat mixed anticoagulation regimen. CRRT treatment parameters, anticoagulant drugs, and infusion doses of calcium and sodium bicarbonate were standardized. The monitoring frequency of peripheral blood gas and activated partial thromboplastin time (APTT) and the criteria for dose stratification adjustment were standardized. Data including patients' demographic baseline data, CRRT treatment duration, filter service life, blood gas electrolytes, dynamic changes of APTT, pipeline and filter coagulation, bleeding and metabolic adverse events, organ function and clinical outcomes were collected for summary and analysis. RESULTS: A total of 11 patients with liver failure undergoing CRRT in CVVHDF mode were enrolled in this study, using the low-dose regional citrate combined with nafamostat mixed anticoagulation regimen. After treatment, the median filter life of patients reached 48 (38, 68.75) hours, with no severe pipeline or filter coagulation; there were no significant abnormalities in systemic coagulation indicators. One case (9.1%) had mild oral mucosal bleeding; no severe massive bleeding occurred. Hypocalcemia and metabolic alkalosis were observed in several patients but were not severe, and no citrate accumulation, severe hypocalcemia, or severe acid-base or electrolyte disorders occurred. PCT was lower than baseline (P = 0.005) and APACHE II score was improved (P = 0.011) over the course of ICU treatment; however, all patients simultaneously received antibiotics, vasopressors, source control, and other ICU supportive care, and these changes therefore cannot be attributed to the mixed anticoagulation regimen. Liver and kidney function showed no obvious deterioration. CONCLUSION: In this small, single-center retrospective case series, a low-dose regional citrate combined with nafamostat mixed anticoagulation regimen was feasible to implement in patients with liver failure receiving CRRT. In this cohort, the median filter life was 48 h, no severe filter or pipeline coagulation was observed, and no citrate accumulation, severe hypocalcemia, or severe acid-base or electrolyte disorders occurred; one case (9.1%) had mild bleeding. Because no comparator group was included, whether these observations reflect a benefit of the mixed regimen over conventional RCA, nafamostat alone, systemic heparin, or no anticoagulation cannot be determined. These findings are preliminary and hypothesis-generating and require confirmation in adequately powered, multicenter, prospective controlled trials.

title: Multidrug-resistant Candida auris osteomyelitis treated with fosmanogepix and surgical source control: A report of a case with favorable outcome.
abstract: Candida auris is an emerging fungus that can cause serious infections in hospitalized patients. It is especially concerning because it is often resistant to several of the medicines normally used to treat fungal infections. Bone infections caused by Candida auris are very rare, and there is little information to guide treatment when the organism is resistant to multiple antifungal drugs. We describe the case of a 44-year-old woman with a chronic pressure sore complicated by a severe infection involving the hip and femur caused by a highly drug-resistant strain of Candida auris. The fungus was resistant to the standard antifungal medications typically used for Candida infections. Candida auris was repeatedly recovered from deep surgical specimens, including bone, despite initial treatment and surgical debridement. Successful management required repeated surgical removal of infected bone and soft tissue, followed by reconstruction and careful wound management. Because there were no suitable approved antifungal options, the patient also received fosmanogepix, a newer antifungal medication provided through a special access program. She completed six weeks of fosmanogepix therapy, which was given as part of a combined treatment approach that included three surgical debridements and definitive wound reconstruction. At the end of antifungal therapy, the wound was continuing to heal and there were no clinical signs of active infection. Healing continued after treatment was stopped, and no recurrence was identified during 12 months of follow-up. This case highlights the importance of aggressive surgical source control in the management of Candida auris osteomyelitis and suggests that fosmanogepix may have a role as part of a combined medical and surgical approach when standard antifungal therapies are not suitable. Further studies are needed to better define the effectiveness, optimal duration, and role of fosmanogepix in bone and joint infections.

sourceName: VA Office of Research and Development
abstract: Multidrug-resistant organisms (MDROs) cause serious infections that are difficult to treat, leading to increased morbidity and mortality, longer hospital stays, and increased healthcare costs. Many risk factors for MDRO infections are present in the Veteran population (such as older age, underlying medical conditions like diabetes, and stays in long-term healthcare settings). Some people can carry these organisms in their gut. Even without current symptoms, carrying these MDROs also increases risk of future infection. Effective, easy to use, and inexpensive interventions to reduce gut carriage of MDROs are needed to reduce risk of infection. Dietary fiber prebiotics have shown promise in improving the healthy gut microbiome, and the investigators have found that individuals with high fiber in their diets have reduced carriage of MDROs in the gut. The investigators propose a randomized controlled trial to test the effectiveness of a dietary fiber prebiotic intervention (resistant potato starch) in reducing gut MDRO carriage in Veterans with a history of MDRO carriage and/or infection. The investigators will also evaluate the effect on the gut microbiome as well as Veterans' experience with the fiber intervention.

abstract: BACKGROUND: Ceftazidime/avibactam (CZA) resistance in KPC-producing Klebsiella pneumoniae is a critical public health threat, traditionally associated with in vivo selection. In this three-year study conducted in an Intensive Care Unit (ICU), we aimed to investigate the emergence of CZA-resistant (CZA-R) K. pneumoniae in patients treated with CZA, assessing the possible role of hospital outbreaks in dissemination. METHODS: We analysed a three-year dataset of antibiotic consumption and K. pneumoniae isolates collected from ICU patients receiving CZA therapy. Whole-genome sequencing (Illumina/Oxford Nanopore) and epidemiological reconstruction were used to investigate resistance mechanisms, KPC variants, and transmission dynamics, including outbreak detection. RESULTS: Among 871 ICU patients, 17.9% received CZA therapy, and 9% of these tested positive for CZA-resistant strains. We identified eight distinct KPC variants, including the novel KPC-295. While in vivo evolution remained the primary driver (71.4%), epidemiological reconstruction revealed that 28.6% of resistant isolates resulted from horizontal transmission, forming three distinct outbreaks of KPC-31, KPC-62, and KPC-66 producers. Alarmingly, 76.2% of CZA-R isolates exhibited co-resistance to FDC, a phenomenon linked to the presence of KPC variants conferring CZA resistance and likely enhanced by the fec operon. These clones persisted in the hospital environment and gut reservoirs of CZA-naive patients. CONCLUSIONS: Our findings suggest that CZA-R outbreaks may be underreported due to difficulties in KPC variant diagnostics and outbreak reconstruction. The emergence of co-resistance to CZA and FDC severely limits treatment options and poses major challenges for patient care and antimicrobial stewardship. These findings underscore the need for strengthened infection prevention and control measures, including early microbiological detection, active surveillance, and prompt containment strategies in ICU settings.

title: Challenges in monitoring and titration of argatroban versus unfractionated heparin in extracorporeal membrane oxygenation.
abstract: OBJECTIVES: Anticoagulation during extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO) remains challenging. Direct thrombin inhibitors such as argatroban are increasingly proposed as alternatives to unfractionated heparin (UFH). We sought to characterize the dose titration and monitoring reliability of argatroban compared with UFH in adult patients who received ECMO. METHODS: This prespecified subanalysis of a randomized controlled pilot trial (2021-2024) included 40 adults on venovenous or venoarterial ECMO randomized to argatroban (target diluted thrombin time 0.6-0.8 μg/mL; n = 20) or UFH (target anti-factor Xa 0.2-0.3 IU/mL; n = 20). The primary outcome was the pooled proportion of measurements within the therapeutic target range. Secondary outcomes included dose requirements, time to target, dose-assay correlations, and platelet count trajectories. RESULTS: Patients who were treated with argatroban achieved therapeutic targets significantly less often than those receiving UFH (38% vs 51% of pooled active measurements; CONCLUSIONS: In this hypothesis-generating subanalysis, patients receiving argatroban achieved therapeutic targets less reliably than those receiving UFH. However, this variability likely reflects challenges in dosing strategy optimization and differing target stringencies rather than intrinsic pharmacokinetic instability of the drug.

title: COPD and Aspergillus—a complex interaction of global health importance.
Global genomic surveillance and temporal trends of carbapenemase-encoding β-lactamase genes in Klebsiella pneumoniae using NCBI pathogen detection data.
abstract: The global spread of carbapenem-resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae is weakening the effectiveness of last-resort antibiotics and making severe infections increasingly difficult to treat. This study examined the geographical distribution, temporal patterns and co-occurrence of carbapenemase genes among K. pneumoniae genome assemblies deposited in the National Center for Biotechnology Information Pathogen Detection database. Genome metadata and antimicrobial resistance genotype information were retrieved between January and February 2026. After data cleaning, 67,057 unique genome assemblies from 123 countries contributed 77,975 carbapenemase-gene detections. Gene frequencies were summarised by continent, country, year and sample source. Poisson and negative binomial regression models were used to examine temporal patterns from 2013 to 2025. Genome-level co-occurrence was assessed using phi correlation coefficients, Jaccard similarity, odds ratios and Fisher's exact tests. blaKPC was the most frequently detected gene, with 39,832 detections (51.08%), followed by blaNDM with 24,412 (31.31%). blaNDM was the dominant gene in Africa, accounting for 1,101 detections (52.68%), whereas blaKPC was dominant in the Americas, Asia, Europe and Oceania, accounting for 59.29%, 56.50%, 38.37% and 38.77% of detections, respectively. Urine and blood were the main sample sources, representing approximately 30% and 22% of the analysed genomes, respectively. Yearly trend analysis showed increases in blaNDM, blaOXA-232 and blaOXA-181. The strongest negative association was found between blaKPC and blaNDM (φ = -0.69), although genomes carrying either gene frequently contained additional antimicrobial resistance genes. These findings demonstrate clear geographical and temporal differences in carbapenemase genes among genome assemblies deposited in NCBI pathogen detection. However, differences in sequencing capacity and database submissions across countries and years should be considered when interpreting the findings. Continued genomic surveillance, antimicrobial stewardship and stronger infection prevention and control measures are needed, particularly in underrepresented regions.

title: Trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole vs. Clindamycin for the Treatment of Children With Invasive MRSA Infections
abstract: The goal of this clinical trial is to learn if trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole (TMP-SMX) works to treat invasive infections due to methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) in children. It will also learn about the safety of TMP-SMX in the treatment of children with invasive MRSA infections. The main questions it aims to answer are: -Is TMP-SMX effective at successfully treating children with invasive infections due to MRSA? What are the side effects of TMP-SMX in children taking it for invasive infections due to MRSA? Researchers will compare TMP-SMX to a clindamycin (a commonly prescribed antibiotic for the treatment of MRSA in children) to see if TMP-SMX works better, worse or the same as clindamycin for children with invasive infections due to MRSA. Participants will: Take TMP-SMX or clindamycin for the treatment of their invasive infection due to MRSA. Will follow up with the provider treating their invasive infection at the discretion of the treating provider. Keep a diary of their symptoms and any side effects of the medicine
